title: externalTrafficPolicy: Local keeps the client’s address but splits traffic by node, not by pod

steps.title: 4 pods on three nodes behind one load balancer
steps.line: The load balancer sends to nodes; each node’s rules pick a pod.
steps.caption: A Service of type LoadBalancer: a cloud load balancer sends outside requests to the nodes, and rules that kube-proxy writes on each node hand every request to a pod. Node 1 runs 3 pods, Node 2 runs 1 and Node 3 runs none. The setting chooses externalTrafficPolicy: Local.
steps.picture: Architecture diagram: 8 services, 7 edges; 4 labelled values.

steps.title: Under Local, each node’s rules list only its own pods
steps.line: Probabilities 1/(n−i) give each pod 1/3 of the node’s requests.
steps.caption: In iptables mode kube-proxy writes one rule per pod. Rule i of n matches with probability 1/(n−i), and the last always matches, so each pod gets 1/n. Under Local Node 1 lists only its 3 pods: 1/3, 1/2, always, so each gets 1/3 of what Node 1 receives.
steps.picture: Architecture diagram: 8 services, 7 edges; Code, 4 lines. Note: “1/3” beside Pod a; “1/3” beside Pod b; “1/3” beside Pod c; chain shown: Node 1 · 10.240.0.1; and 3 more. New in this step: Code, 4 lines.

steps.title: Node 3 runs no pod, so it fails the health check
steps.line: Node 1 and Node 2 answer 200 and each get 1/2 of requests.
steps.caption: Under Local, kube-proxy answers the load balancer’s health check on each node: 200 when the node runs a pod of the Service, 503 when it runs none. The load balancer stops sending to Node 3, so Node 1 and Node 2 each get 1/2 of the requests.
steps.picture: Architecture diagram: 8 services, 7 edges. Note: “200, 3 local pods” beside Node 1 · 10.240.0.1; “200, 1 local pod” beside Node 2 · 10.240.0.2; “503, 0 local pods” beside Node 3 · 10.240.0.3; fails the health check: Node 3 · 10.240.0.3.

steps.title: The request stays on its node and keeps the client’s address
steps.line: Pod a sees 198.51.100.79: no source NAT and no second hop.
steps.caption: Node 1’s rules list only its own pods, so the request never leaves Node 1, and kube-proxy adds no source NAT for it. Pod a sees the client’s address, 198.51.100.79. Under Local no outside request takes a second hop.
steps.picture: Architecture diagram: 8 services, 7 edges. Note: “from 198.51.100.79” beside Pod a; travelled: Load balancer → Node 1 · 10.240.0.1; Node 1 · 10.240.0.1 → Pod a; focused: Node 1 · 10.240.0.1; and 3 more.

steps.title: Pod d gets 1/2 of the requests; pods a, b and c get 1/6 each
steps.line: Split by node, not pod: each node with pods gets 1/2.
steps.caption: The load balancer splits by node, not by pod: Node 1 and Node 2 each get 1/2. Node 1 splits its 1/2 three ways; Node 2 sends all of its 1/2 to pod d, so pod d gets 3 times as many requests as pod a.
steps.picture: Architecture diagram: 8 services, 7 edges. Note: “16.7%” beside Pod a; “16.7%” beside Pod b; “16.7%” beside Pod c; and 1 more.

steps.title: With 3, 1, 0 pods, Local trades even load for the client’s address
steps.line: Cluster sends 2 in 3 requests to another node; Local sends none.
steps.caption: Cluster spreads requests evenly over the pods, but 2 in 3 cross to another node and every pod sees a node’s address. Local keeps each request on its node with the client’s address. The load balancer weighs nodes, not pods, so pod d takes 3 times the load of pod a.
steps.picture: Architecture diagram: 8 services, 7 edges; “Cluster”, 3 labelled values; “Local”, 4 labelled values. New in this step: “Cluster”, 3 labelled values; “Local”, 4 labelled values.

steps.title: What these shares leave out
steps.line: Shares are iptables-mode averages; IPVS defaults to round robin.
steps.caption: The shares are long-run averages for kube-proxy’s iptables mode; IPVS mode defaults to round robin. kube-proxy’s health check reports each node’s pod count in a header, but the docs warn that some cloud load balancers cannot weight nodes. Topology-aware routing and session affinity are left out.

steps.title: Each node’s rules pick one of all 4 pods

steps.title: Under Cluster, 2 in 3 requests leave the node they reach
steps.line: Node 3 sends this request on to pod d on Node 2.
steps.caption: Each node gets a third of the requests and picks among all 4 pods. A request leaves its node when the pick runs elsewhere: 1 in 4 on Node 1, 3 in 4 on Node 2, all on Node 3. Here Node 3 sends one to pod d on Node 2.

steps.title: The pod sees the node’s address, not the client’s
steps.line: Node 3 swaps 198.51.100.79 for its own address, 10.240.0.3.
steps.caption: Under Cluster, kube-proxy marks every outside request for source NAT, in case it crosses nodes. Node 3 replaces the client’s address, 198.51.100.79, with its own, 10.240.0.3, and pod d sees that. Requests that stay on their node are rewritten too.
